Drosophila melanogaster with wings and antennae that flies

where this clade is recorded and what is recorded as eating it

chain.requirement: A longer intrinsic lifespan: the design must change the organism's own age-specific hazard rate, not merely its observed survival in a protected vial.
chain.species_caveat: Unusually for this project the proxy and the target are the same species: every link below is Drosophila melanogaster data, but it is laboratory-strain data (wDah, w1118, yw) from GAL4/GeneSwitch transgenics in vials, not from the designed construct, and several links are female-only.

missing_rungs.why: No source fetched in this run reports a hazard-RATE parameter for any of these genotypes. Every link except l15 reports median or maximum lifespan, and l15's statement ('reduced late age-specific mortality') is qualitative and was read in an abstract only. The run's performance layer needs an intrinsic hazard; nothing here supplies a number for it.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A demographic study fitting Gompertz (or Gompertz-Makeham) parameters A and B to large cohorts of a defined long-lived genotype and its matched control, with the fitted values reported, so that a genotype edit can be mapped to a change in baseline hazard rather than to a percentage change in median lifespan.

missing_rungs.why: On the strongest tissue-restricted arm (dFOXO in median neurosecretory cells, l08) the mediator is explicitly unknown: Alic 2014 found no significant change in dilp2, dilp3 or dilp5 mRNA, so the DILP2 route established in l05-l07 is not the route used there, and the signal is called 'as-yet-unidentified'.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: An unbiased secretome or haemolymph proteomic comparison of mNSC>dfoxo flies versus controls, followed by RNAi of each candidate in the mNSCs to test whether it is required for the lifespan extension.

missing_rungs.why: No direct biochemical demonstration of InR-to-dFOXO signalling in Drosophila was obtained. The canonical paper (Puig et al. 2003, Genes Dev) is not open access: Europe PMC fullTextXML returned HTTP 500 and the NCBI PMC efetch body states that the publisher does not allow full-text XML download. Jünger 2003 (l01, l03) is genetic epistasis plus localisation, not kinase biochemistry, and its 14-3-3 statement cites mammalian work.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Access to Puig et al. 2003 (or equivalent open-access Drosophila work) showing phospho-site-specific dFOXO regulation by dPKB/Akt downstream of InR, with reporter or ChIP evidence for the target genes.

missing_rungs.why: The whole TOR arm (l11-l13) has no cell, cell_cell, tissue or organ rung at all. Rapamycin was fed to whole animals and the 4E-BP null is constitutive and ubiquitous. Nothing fetched in this run places TOR-dependent lifespan control in a named Drosophila tissue.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Tissue-restricted, adult-onset TORC1 manipulation (for example fat-body-, gut- or neuron-specific Tor RNAi or Rheb/TSC manipulation under GeneSwitch control) with lifespan readout.

missing_rungs.why: The 'cell' rung is never actually resolved to cells. Every fat-body result is qPCR, western blot or immunoassay on dissected tissue or whole flies, with the cell type inferred from a GAL4 driver's reported expression pattern rather than measured per cell.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Single-cell or single-nucleus RNA-seq of adult fat body and brain under the same dfoxo induction, so that the responding cell populations (and the fraction of them responding) are measured rather than assumed from a driver.

missing_rungs.why: Nothing fetched connects any of this mechanism to EXTRINSIC mortality. The run's performance layer caps expected life in the wild at 12.5 days through extrinsic hazard; every experiment cited here was done in vials with food, no predation and no weather, so the ladder explains only the intrinsic term and cannot predict the 1.09x wild outcome.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Field or mesocosm survival data for a reduced-IIS Drosophila genotype against a matched control under natural extrinsic mortality, or at minimum a laboratory hazard decomposition under imposed extrinsic mortality.

missing_rungs.why: Sex specificity is unexplained and unmodelled. Giannakou 2004 reports fat-body dFOXO extends female but not male life-span, Bai 2012's dilp6 effects are female-only, Alic 2014's experiments are female-only, and Bjedov 2010 reports a smaller rapamycin effect in males. A design requirement stated as 'a longer lifespan' is therefore under-specified.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Matched male and female cohorts for each tissue-restricted intervention, and a mechanistic account of the sex difference (for example whether the fat-body-to-brain DILP6/DILP2 circuit operates in males at all).

missing_rungs.why: ADDED BY VERIFICATION. The cell_cell -> tissue rung is circular and reverses direction. l05 leaves the fat body cell (CL_0000565) and lands on the fat-body-to-IPC interaction; l06 then lands that interaction back on FBbt_00003209, adult fat body - the same tissue the walk departed from one rung earlier - and points the arrow fat-body-ward, against the fat-body -> brain direction of l05 and l07. So the walk formally advances a level while physically standing still, and the single link that carries the whole ladder across this level (l06, Hwangbo 2004) is 'abstract only' because the paper is not open access. Every other rung on the walkable path has full text behind it; this one does not.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A full-text, tissue-restricted source whose cell-cell step lands on a tissue the chain has not already used - for example a brain or neurosecretory-tissue readout downstream of the fat body DILP6 signal - so that the cell_cell rung carries the walk forward rather than back onto its own origin.

missing_rungs.why: ADDED BY VERIFICATION. FBbt_00003209 (adult fat body) occupies BOTH the tissue rung (l06 target, l07 source) and the organ rung (l09 source). One ontology id standing at two consecutive levels means the tissue -> organ step is not a real level transition for the fat body arm; l09's note states the fly fat body is both, but the consequence - that the ladder has six distinct entities across seven rungs - was not recorded as a break.

That is correct behaviour and it is the whole finding: there is no scenario, no metric and no threshold anywhere in this engine for how long an organism lives.

unparsed.of_clause: I want a fruit fly that lives longer
unparsed.reason: organism "fruit fly" has no reference parameter set in this engine (it holds measured parameters for: zebrafish, flying fish, winged zebrafish, wingless flying fish, TFF, the ff-zf chimera). It is not mapped to a "close" one, because the nearest fish is not this animal. A taxon-based design can still be built from it: see spec.taxon, organism_create {taxon} and organism_from_blueprint. The rest of this clause IS parsed: any criterion in it is on the spec, and will be judged once a parameter set for this clade exists.

numbers.a_bug_this_run_found: Before this run the same sentence produced a GLIDE criterion. familyGlide matches the free-standing word "fly", `fruit fly` contains one, and the parser read the name of the animal as a requirement that it be able to fly -- a criterion nobody asked for, attached to a request about lifespan. Two-word insect names ending in "fly" are now organism names and are taken out of the clause before the criterion families read it.

checks.body: the front door now ROUTES the requirement instead of dropping it: 0 requirement(s) for physics_check, 1 for performance_check, 0 that no layer takes. "lives longer" goes to performance_check { kind: "lifespan" }, and the quantities that check needs are the designer's to declare. Before this the whole clause came back unparsed, which read as a parse failure when it was a capability gap -- two different things the routing block now tells apart.

performance_criteria.how: performance_check { kind: "lifespan", ... } -- the quantities it needs are the designer's to declare, with sources

routing.structures: organism-design/blueprint.mjs reads the structures named in the text and resolves them to Uberon/CL terms for the taxon; organism_from_blueprint brings the result into the studio
routing.laws: lean_check decides clade scope from the taxon and reports every law as holds / violated / out-of-scope / cannot-evaluate
routing.movement: locomotion_check -- how it moves, which no part list can settle: the scallop theorem, the cycle arithmetic and the Reynolds/Froude regimes
routing.world: ecology_check -- where the clade is recorded, what else is there, and what is recorded eating it. It will not predict exclusion without declared population parameters.

unparsed.reason: organism "fruit fly" has no reference parameter set in this engine (it holds measured parameters for: zebrafish, flying fish, winged zebrafish, wingless flying fish, TFF, the ff-zf chimera). It is not mapped to a "close" one, because the nearest fish is not this animal. A taxon-based design can still be built from it: see spec.taxon, organism_create {taxon} and organism_from_blueprint. The rest of this clause IS parsed: any criterion in it is on the spec, and will be judged once a parameter set for this clade exists.
unparsed.verdict: the organism has no reference parameter set; declare one with organism_create { taxon, declared }

routing.summary: 0 requirement(s) for physics_check, 1 for performance_check, 0 that no layer takes.

checks.body: 12 scenario modules exist and 0 of them measure anything like a lifespan: none. The scenarios are glide, current, temperature, depth, altitude, predator, grip and the rest -- every one of them a question asked of an organism at an age, not a question about how many ages it gets. The engine has growth tracks (ontogeny.json, for two teleosts) and no senescence model for anything. There is no mortality rate, no survival curve and no cause of death in this repository.

numbers.searched_for: lifespan, senescence, longevity, mortality, ageing -- across sim-engine/ and the Lean law set

scaling.how: A part is drawn at (L/L0)^e, with e = 1 for a length, 2 for a surface and 3 for a volume.
scaling.under: isometry, a HYPOTHESIS the design makes and not a property of any organism
scaling.falsified_for: E1 records that measured fin area in Cypselurus hiraii does NOT scale isometrically, so for that one body this hypothesis is known to be false and the drawing is known to be wrong in a named way.

order_of_appearance.why: Nothing in sim-engine or the Lean law set predicts when a part appears. genotype-developmental-ordering certifies that a DECLARED ordering has no cycle; E7 says a trait appearing after a lethal stage cannot be scored. Neither supplies an order.
order_of_appearance.what_would_be_needed: a staged expression or morphology dataset for the organism, and a rule mapping a stage to a part. For every organism in these runs that dataset does not exist.

timeline.not_a_simulation: This is a declared growth track being drawn, not development being simulated. No cell divides, no tissue forms and nothing moves; the body is redrawn larger.
timeline.note: no generation of this run created an organism with declared parameters, so the engine resolved no STATE and there is no age axis. The body is drawn at one unspecified moment.

basis_legend.proof: a Lean theorem, kernel-checked, with a module and a line
basis_legend.check: arithmetic in sim-engine/validate/, resting on something undisputed but not formalised
basis_legend.literature: a graded, quoted link from a paper, usually in another species
basis_legend.declared: a number a person typed, carrying the source string that says they typed it

honesty: The molecular rungs are LITERATURE in Drosophila melanogaster, each link graded and quoted. Unusually for this project the proxy and the target are the same species: every link below is Drosophila melanogaster data, but it is laboratory-strain data (wDah, w1118, yw) from GAL4/GeneSwitch transgenics in vials, not from the designed construct, and several links are female-only.

Rung organ -> phenotype is MISSING: No source fetched in this run reports a hazard-RATE parameter for any of these genotypes. Every link except l15 reports median or maximum lifespan, and l15's statement ('reduced late age-specific mortality') is qualitative and was read in an abstract only. The run's performance layer needs an intrinsic hazard; nothing here supplies a number for it.

Rung cell_cell -> tissue is MISSING: On the strongest tissue-restricted arm (dFOXO in median neurosecretory cells, l08) the mediator is explicitly unknown: Alic 2014 found no significant change in dilp2, dilp3 or dilp5 mRNA, so the DILP2 route established in l05-l07 is not the route used there, and the signal is called 'as-yet-unidentified'.

Rung molecule -> pathway is MISSING: No direct biochemical demonstration of InR-to-dFOXO signalling in Drosophila was obtained. The canonical paper (Puig et al. 2003, Genes Dev) is not open access: Europe PMC fullTextXML returned HTTP 500 and the NCBI PMC efetch body states that the publisher does not allow full-text XML download. Jünger 2003 (l01, l03) is genetic epistasis plus localisation, not kinase biochemistry, and its 14-3-3 statement cites mammalian work.

Rung pathway -> cell is MISSING: The whole TOR arm (l11-l13) has no cell, cell_cell, tissue or organ rung at all. Rapamycin was fed to whole animals and the 4E-BP null is constitutive and ubiquitous. Nothing fetched in this run places TOR-dependent lifespan control in a named Drosophila tissue.

Rung cell -> cell_cell is MISSING: The 'cell' rung is never actually resolved to cells. Every fat-body result is qPCR, western blot or immunoassay on dissected tissue or whole flies, with the cell type inferred from a GAL4 driver's reported expression pattern rather than measured per cell.

Rung phenotype -> phenotype is MISSING: Nothing fetched connects any of this mechanism to EXTRINSIC mortality. The run's performance layer caps expected life in the wild at 12.5 days through extrinsic hazard; every experiment cited here was done in vials with food, no predation and no weather, so the ladder explains only the intrinsic term and cannot predict the 1.09x wild outcome.

Rung organ -> phenotype is MISSING: Sex specificity is unexplained and unmodelled. Giannakou 2004 reports fat-body dFOXO extends female but not male life-span, Bai 2012's dilp6 effects are female-only, Alic 2014's experiments are female-only, and Bjedov 2010 reports a smaller rapamycin effect in males. A design requirement stated as 'a longer lifespan' is therefore under-specified.

Rung cell_cell -> tissue is MISSING: ADDED BY VERIFICATION. The cell_cell -> tissue rung is circular and reverses direction. l05 leaves the fat body cell (CL_0000565) and lands on the fat-body-to-IPC interaction; l06 then lands that interaction back on FBbt_00003209, adult fat body - the same tissue the walk departed from one rung earlier - and points the arrow fat-body-ward, against the fat-body -> brain direction of l05 and l07. So the walk formally advances a level while physically standing still, and the single link that carries the whole ladder across this level (l06, Hwangbo 2004) is 'abstract only' because the paper is not open access. Every other rung on the walkable path has full text behind it; this one does not.

Rung tissue -> organ is MISSING: ADDED BY VERIFICATION. FBbt_00003209 (adult fat body) occupies BOTH the tissue rung (l06 target, l07 source) and the organ rung (l09 source). One ontology id standing at two consecutive levels means the tissue -> organ step is not a real level transition for the fat body arm; l09's note states the fly fat body is both, but the consequence - that the ladder has six distinct entities across seven rungs - was not recorded as a break.

0.what_it_taught: The request is about time-to-death, which no SCENARIO measures and no law covers -- and it is no longer a dead end. The parser reads it as a lifespan requirement and the routing block sends it to performance_check, the layer built for exactly the three things these runs asked for that nothing could express.

frame.THIS_IS_NOT_MORPHOMETRY: Every position here is DECLARED by this file, not measured from any specimen and not derived from any ontology. A slot says 'the eye goes near the front of the head, on both sides'; it does not say how big a fly's eye is or where it sits in millimetres. The only morphometric geometry in this repository is anatomy-model/parametric, which builds one teleost from Park and Choi's measurements. Nothing here should ever be read off as a measurement, and the theatre view labels every part with this basis.

blueprint-well-formedness.label: An emitted anatomical blueprint graph is well-formed under its own rules
blueprint-well-formedness.about: the part graph itself: that each term is a node, each parent relation is one Uberon or CL relation, and the graph has no cycle
blueprint-well-formedness.how: Structural only. It certifies that the blueprint is a well-formed graph over ontology terms — it says nothing about whether the part could exist, work, or bear a load. It is the one law in the set that reaches every part of every organism, and the weakest thing anyone could want to know about any of them.

thompson1917-ch03-07.label: Weight tends to vary as the cube of linear dimensions during growth
thompson1917-ch03-07.about: the slope of log mass against log length is 3 under isometry
thompson1917-ch03-07.how: The cube law as an exponent, which makes it testable: a measured slope that is not 3 is a measurement of how the organism departs from isometry. E1 is the observation that this project's fish do depart.

altitude-coupling.label: Demand rises and supply falls with height together, so the flyable heights reach down to the ground
altitude-coupling.about: that the feasible set is downward closed in altitude: feasible high implies feasible low
altitude-coupling.how: Couples the two layers: thinner air both reduces lift and reduces oxygen, so a design feasible at altitude is feasible below it. Useful mainly as a sanity direction on a scenario sweep.

physiology-q10.label: Q10 temperature scaling: the ratio between two temperatures is Q10 raised to their difference over ten
physiology-q10.about: how a rate changes with a ten-degree change in temperature
physiology-q10.how: Proved, no instance: no candidate commits a Q10 and the conditions file fixes 25 C. Every rate in every run is therefore at one temperature, and a design whose selling point is a rate should say which temperature it means.

genotype-developmental-ordering.label: No structure develops from a precursor that appears later than it does
genotype-developmental-ordering.about: that a claimed developmental ordering has no cycle and respects the dependencies declared for it
genotype-developmental-ordering.how: The only law in the set that is about TIME, which makes it the one the time-lapse rests on. It certifies that an ordering is consistent; it does not supply one, does not predict a rate, and says nothing about how long a stage takes. A developmental animation is therefore a declared ordering being checked for consistency, never a simulation of development.

E2.label: The fitted mass exponent lies in [2.90, 3.02]
E2.about: a measured band for the weight ratio
E2.how: A measured band from one species. Outside that species it is a number, not a constraint.

E7.label: A lever lethal before the scoring stage cannot produce the phenotype
E7.about: that a trait appearing after a lethal stage cannot be scored
E7.how: The other law about time, and the one that matters most for a time-lapse: a part that appears after the organism would have died is not a part. Pairs with the developmental ordering law.

physiology-laplace.label: Laplace wall stress: pressure in a thin-walled vessel is limited by wall strength, thickness and radius
physiology-laplace.about: the pressure a thin-walled tube or sphere can hold, from radius, wall thickness and wall strength
physiology-laplace.how: Proved, with NO INSTANCE anywhere in this project: no vessel radius, wall thickness or wall strength exists for any organism here. It is in this table so that a part it would constrain carries the chip that says which three numbers are missing — a law with no instance is a request for data, and silence about it is worse.

scaling-strength-law.label: Strength scales as L^2: the missing half of Galileo's square-cube argument (R7)
scaling-strength-law.about: breaking load under isometry: it scales as L squared while weight scales as L cubed
scaling-strength-law.how: The reason a design cannot simply be made bigger. Weight grows faster than the cross-section carrying it, so a part that holds at one size fails at another with no change in material or shape.

elastic-similarity.label: Elastic similarity scaling (not formalised)
elastic-similarity.about: scaling that holds elastic deflection constant instead of stress
elastic-similarity.how: NOT FORMALISED. The named alternative to isometry for real skeletons, so its absence is why every scaling chip here says `under isometry`.

scaling-area-law.label: Area law and wing loading under isometry (R2, R3)
scaling-area-law.about: area under isometry: A scales as L squared
scaling-area-law.how: If the design scales a lifting or exchange surface by changing a length, this fixes the area ratio it gets — under isometry, which is a hypothesis about the design, not a fact about the animal. The flying-fish audit returns `violated` here for skin and fins, because that fish is NOT isometric: the law is right and the hypothesis is false, which is the useful outcome.

scaling-bending-law.label: Bending strength of an isometric member via the section modulus (R9)
scaling-bending-law.about: bending stress in a cantilever as the body scales
scaling-bending-law.how: A wing or a leg held out from the body is a cantilever, and the stress at its root rises with size under isometry. This is the law that should be consulted first by anyone who wants to put a lifting surface on the end of a limb.

thompson1917-ch02-10.label: Speed varies as the square root of linear size in swimming, flight and walking
thompson1917-ch02-10.about: how minimum flight speed scales with size
thompson1917-ch02-10.how: A bigger animal of the same shape must fly faster to stay up. Combined with a launch speed the design declares, this is often what decides a flight claim.

flight-allometry-law.label: General allometry: measured exponents compose (W = a L^b)
flight-allometry-law.about: minimum speed from wing loading and a maximum lift coefficient
flight-allometry-law.how: The law behind `lifting_area_supports_mass`. It needs a maximum lift coefficient, which is where a design most often stops: the coefficient is a MEASURED property of a real wing, the table of them is scoped by clade, and borrowing one across clades is the failure that table exists to prevent.

flight-climb-glide-law.label: Climb from excess power and the range of a steady glide
flight-climb-glide-law.about: climb rate from excess power, and the horizontal range of a steady glide from a height
flight-climb-glide-law.how: Scope.taxa is `any`: it is a theorem about a model and applies wherever the design supplies the quantities and accepts the hypotheses. That makes it the most portable flight law here — and it is about a GLIDE. Powered flight is a power question and goes to the aerobic bound.

aspect-ratio-induced-drag.label: Induced drag falls with wing aspect ratio (not formalised)
aspect-ratio-induced-drag.about: induced drag falling with aspect ratio
aspect-ratio-induced-drag.how: NOT FORMALISED. Without it, nothing here distinguishes a long narrow wing from a short broad one of the same area, which is most of what a wing design IS.

genotype-pleiotropy-closure.label: An edit to a gene must be shown changing every node the map links that gene to
genotype-pleiotropy-closure.about: what a view of a genotype may omit: that the set shown is closed under the declared pleiotropy relation
genotype-pleiotropy-closure.how: A statement about the COMPLETENESS OF A VIEW, not about development. If a molecule is shown as affecting one part, this is what certifies that its other declared effects were not quietly dropped from the picture — which is exactly the failure a per-part panel invites.

genotype-genetic-code.label: A claimed amino-acid change is impossible below the code distance
genotype-genetic-code.about: what a claimed set of substitutions rules out, given the genetic code
genotype-genetic-code.how: Operates on a claimed edit. For a construct with an unedited donor genome there is nothing for it to operate on, and that is the honest answer rather than a refusal.

gene-regulatory-dynamics.label: Gene regulatory dynamics (not formalised)
gene-regulatory-dynamics.about: the dynamics of a regulatory network
gene-regulatory-dynamics.how: NOT FORMALISED, and it is the hole the whole scale ladder sits over. Nothing in the Lean set connects a molecule to a tissue. The ladder's molecular rungs are therefore LITERATURE, graded and quoted, and the theatre must never draw them in the same colour as a proof.

muscle-power-premise.label: Thompson's muscle-power premise P = f p M (retired)
muscle-power-premise.how: STATED, NOT PROVED: a named hypothesis (MusclePowerLaw in lean/Delphi/Scaling.lean), replaced for the Studio by the aerobic bound. A chip for it must read as an assumption, because that is all it is.

links.downgrade_reason: The quoted sentence is the second half of an explicitly model-level statement: the preceding sentence in ft_PMC333403.xml reads 'In summary, our overexpression experiments are consistent with a model in which, under normal conditions, excess FOXO transcription factor is phosphorylated by dPKB and kept inactive in the cytoplasm.' missing_rungs.why: No source fetched in this run reports a hazard-RATE parameter for any of these genotypes. Every link except l15 reports median or maximum lifespan, and l15's statement ('reduced late age-specific mortality') is qualitative and was read in an abstract only. The run's performance layer needs an intrinsic hazard; nothing here supplies a number for it.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A demographic study fitting Gompertz (or Gompertz-Makeham) parameters A and B to large cohorts of a defined long-lived genotype and its matched control, with the fitted values reported, so that a genotype edit can be mapped to a change in baseline hazard rather than to a percentage change in median lifespan.

missing_rungs.why: On the strongest tissue-restricted arm (dFOXO in median neurosecretory cells, l08) the mediator is explicitly unknown: Alic 2014 found no significant change in dilp2, dilp3 or dilp5 mRNA, so the DILP2 route established in l05-l07 is not the route used there, and the signal is called 'as-yet-unidentified'.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: An unbiased secretome or haemolymph proteomic comparison of mNSC>dfoxo flies versus controls, followed by RNAi of each candidate in the mNSCs to test whether it is required for the lifespan extension.

missing_rungs.why: No direct biochemical demonstration of InR-to-dFOXO signalling in Drosophila was obtained. The canonical paper (Puig et al. 2003, Genes Dev) is not open access: Europe PMC fullTextXML returned HTTP 500 and the NCBI PMC efetch body states that the publisher does not allow full-text XML download. Jünger 2003 (l01, l03) is genetic epistasis plus localisation, not kinase biochemistry, and its 14-3-3 statement cites mammalian work.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Access to Puig et al. 2003 (or equivalent open-access Drosophila work) showing phospho-site-specific dFOXO regulation by dPKB/Akt downstream of InR, with reporter or ChIP evidence for the target genes.

missing_rungs.why: The whole TOR arm (l11-l13) has no cell, cell_cell, tissue or organ rung at all. Rapamycin was fed to whole animals and the 4E-BP null is constitutive and ubiquitous. Nothing fetched in this run places TOR-dependent lifespan control in a named Drosophila tissue.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Tissue-restricted, adult-onset TORC1 manipulation (for example fat-body-, gut- or neuron-specific Tor RNAi or Rheb/TSC manipulation under GeneSwitch control) with lifespan readout.

missing_rungs.why: The 'cell' rung is never actually resolved to cells. Every fat-body result is qPCR, western blot or immunoassay on dissected tissue or whole flies, with the cell type inferred from a GAL4 driver's reported expression pattern rather than measured per cell.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Single-cell or single-nucleus RNA-seq of adult fat body and brain under the same dfoxo induction, so that the responding cell populations (and the fraction of them responding) are measured rather than assumed from a driver.

missing_rungs.why: Nothing fetched connects any of this mechanism to EXTRINSIC mortality. The run's performance layer caps expected life in the wild at 12.5 days through extrinsic hazard; every experiment cited here was done in vials with food, no predation and no weather, so the ladder explains only the intrinsic term and cannot predict the 1.09x wild outcome.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Field or mesocosm survival data for a reduced-IIS Drosophila genotype against a matched control under natural extrinsic mortality, or at minimum a laboratory hazard decomposition under imposed extrinsic mortality.

missing_rungs.why: Sex specificity is unexplained and unmodelled. Giannakou 2004 reports fat-body dFOXO extends female but not male life-span, Bai 2012's dilp6 effects are female-only, Alic 2014's experiments are female-only, and Bjedov 2010 reports a smaller rapamycin effect in males. A design requirement stated as 'a longer lifespan' is therefore under-specified.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Matched male and female cohorts for each tissue-restricted intervention, and a mechanistic account of the sex difference (for example whether the fat-body-to-brain DILP6/DILP2 circuit operates in males at all).

checks.body: Drosophila melanogaster resolves and the hierarchy is substantial: 5 organ systems, 26 organs, 24 tissues, 45 cell types, all Uberon and Cell Ontology terms with the query that produced each one. Every term is a structure. Not one of them is a rate, and lifespan is a rate.

a STATE resolves at each of the four declared stages, and the track is NOT MONOTONIC: egg 1e-8 kg / 0.0005 m, larva 0.0000015 kg / 0.0045 m, pupa 0.0000012 kg / 0.003 m, adult 0.000001 kg / 0.0025 m. The larva is heavier and longer than the adult it becomes, so a growth curve for this animal goes up and then down. Every value carries kind "assumed (declared by the design)" -- declared, not measured -- and nothing here simulates the transition between any two of them.

numbers.what_it_is_not: Four declared masses at four declared ages. No cell divides, no imaginal disc forms, and the only Lean law about time (genotype-developmental-ordering) certifies that a declared ordering is acyclic -- it does not supply one.

checks.about: the resolved state against a released lawset
checks.body: 17 cannot-evaluate, 18 out-of-scope. No law in the set bears on lifespan for any clade, so even a law base written about insects would not have answered this.

mass_kg.source: DESIGN INPUT: order of a milligram. The lifespan claim is about THIS stage and no other. Stated, not measured.

SL_m.source: DESIGN INPUT: order of two and a half millimetres, SHORTER than the larva it came from. Stated, not measured.

ageDays.source: resolved by organism_get at the last declared age

temperature_C.source: resolved by organism_get at the last declared age

rho.source: ambient air density 1.225 kg/m3 from the conditions the engine resolved; a default, not a measurement of anywhere

scaling.how: A part is drawn at (L/L0)^e, with e = 1 for a length, 2 for a surface and 3 for a volume.
scaling.under: isometry, a HYPOTHESIS the design makes and not a property of any organism
scaling.falsified_for: E1 records that measured fin area in Cypselurus hiraii does NOT scale isometrically, so for that one body this hypothesis is known to be false and the drawing is known to be wrong in a named way.

order_of_appearance.why: Nothing in sim-engine or the Lean law set predicts when a part appears. genotype-developmental-ordering certifies that a DECLARED ordering has no cycle; E7 says a trait appearing after a lethal stage cannot be scored. Neither supplies an order.
order_of_appearance.what_would_be_needed: a staged expression or morphology dataset for the organism, and a rule mapping a stage to a part. For every organism in these runs that dataset does not exist.

timeline.not_a_simulation: This is a declared growth track being drawn, not development being simulated. No cell divides, no tissue forms and nothing moves; the body is redrawn larger.

basis_legend.proof: a Lean theorem, kernel-checked, with a module and a line
basis_legend.check: arithmetic in sim-engine/validate/, resting on something undisputed but not formalised
basis_legend.literature: a graded, quoted link from a paper, usually in another species
basis_legend.declared: a number a person typed, carrying the source string that says they typed it

honesty: 3 part(s) are named by the literature chain and ABSENT from the blueprint (fat body cell, adult fat body, adult brain). They are drawn as ghosts, marked blueprint_has_it: false. For the fruit fly these are the very organs the longevity experiments act in.
The 4 molecules are marker annotations from the Protein Ontology, carried by the blueprint. None of them was measured in this organism and none is evidence of function.

So the walk formally advances a level while physically standing still, and the single link that carries the whole ladder across this level (l06, Hwangbo 2004) is 'abstract only' because the paper is not open access. Every other rung on the walkable path has full text behind it; this one does not.

Rung tissue -> organ is MISSING: ADDED BY VERIFICATION. FBbt_00003209 (adult fat body) occupies BOTH the tissue rung (l06 target, l07 source) and the organ rung (l09 source). One ontology id standing at two consecutive levels means the tissue -> organ step is not a real level transition for the fat body arm; l09's note states the fly fat body is both, but the consequence - that the ladder has six distinct entities across seven rungs - was not recorded as a break.
71 law chips are out of scope for this organism: the law is about the right quantity and its numbers belong to another clade.

THE ONTOLOGY BARELY PLACES THIS BODY IN THIS ORGANISM. Of 131 parts the blueprint returned, 2 have an in_taxon restriction specific enough to be evidence that Drosophila melanogaster has them; 44 are restricted only to a clade containing most of the animal kingdom, and 85 carry no restriction at all. The blueprint keeps a part unless a constraint removes it, so most of what is drawn here is unevidenced rather than wrong.
No part in this view has measured geometry. Every position is a declared slot in sim-engine/scales/body-frames.json, and a shape is a primitive, not a morphology.

taxon_audit.headline: Of 131 parts: 2 placed specifically, 44 placed only vacuously, 85 unconstrained, 0 contested, 0 forbidden. Only the first number is evidence that a part belongs in Drosophila melanogaster.
taxon_audit.what_it_shows: Taxon constraints cannot do the work the blueprint layer asks of them. The blueprint keeps a part unless a constraint removes it, and for the great majority of parts the ontology either says nothing at all or says only that the part occurs somewhere in a clade containing most of the animal kingdom. That is why a fruit fly came back with bone marrow and a preen gland and without a brain: nothing in the pipeline was ever in a position to object.

verdicts.placed: some in_taxon restriction includes this organism
verdicts.contested: there IS an in_taxon restriction and none includes this organism -- a defect in the blueprint
verdicts.placed-vacuously: the only in_taxon restriction is to a clade in the top third of this organism lineage -- true of it and of most animals, so it discriminates nothing
verdicts.unconstrained: no in_taxon restriction exists, so the ontology is silent; not a defect and not a licence
verdicts.forbidden: never_in_taxon asserts this part cannot be in this organism

frame.THIS_IS_NOT_MORPHOMETRY: Every position here is DECLARED by this file, not measured from any specimen and not derived from any ontology. blueprint-well-formedness.label: An emitted anatomical blueprint graph is well-formed under its own rules
blueprint-well-formedness.about: the part graph itself: that each term is a node, each parent relation is one Uberon or CL relation, and the graph has no cycle
blueprint-well-formedness.how: Structural only. It certifies that the blueprint is a well-formed graph over ontology terms — it says nothing about whether the part could exist, work, or bear a load. It is the one law in the set that reaches every part of every organism, and the weakest thing anyone could want to know about any of them.

thompson1917-ch03-07.label: Weight tends to vary as the cube of linear dimensions during growth
thompson1917-ch03-07.about: the slope of log mass against log length is 3 under isometry
thompson1917-ch03-07.how: The cube law as an exponent, which makes it testable: a measured slope that is not 3 is a measurement of how the organism departs from isometry. E1 is the observation that this project's fish do depart.

altitude-coupling.label: Demand rises and supply falls with height together, so the flyable heights reach down to the ground
altitude-coupling.about: that the feasible set is downward closed in altitude: feasible high implies feasible low
altitude-coupling.how: Couples the two layers: thinner air both reduces lift and reduces oxygen, so a design feasible at altitude is feasible below it. Useful mainly as a sanity direction on a scenario sweep.

physiology-q10.label: Q10 temperature scaling: the ratio between two temperatures is Q10 raised to their difference over ten
physiology-q10.about: how a rate changes with a ten-degree change in temperature
physiology-q10.how: Proved, no instance: no candidate commits a Q10 and the conditions file fixes 25 C. Every rate in every run is therefore at one temperature, and a design whose selling point is a rate should say which temperature it means.

genotype-developmental-ordering.label: No structure develops from a precursor that appears later than it does
genotype-developmental-ordering.about: that a claimed developmental ordering has no cycle and respects the dependencies declared for it
genotype-developmental-ordering.how: The only law in the set that is about TIME, which makes it the one the time-lapse rests on. It certifies that an ordering is consistent; it does not supply one, does not predict a rate, and says nothing about how long a stage takes. A developmental animation is therefore a declared ordering being checked for consistency, never a simulation of development.

E2.label: The fitted mass exponent lies in [2.90, 3.02]
E2.about: a measured band for the weight ratio
E2.how: A measured band from one species. Outside that species it is a number, not a constraint.

E7.label: A lever lethal before the scoring stage cannot produce the phenotype
E7.about: that a trait appearing after a lethal stage cannot be scored
E7.how: The other law about time, and the one that matters most for a time-lapse: a part that appears after the organism would have died is not a part. Pairs with the developmental ordering law.

physiology-laplace.label: Laplace wall stress: pressure in a thin-walled vessel is limited by wall strength, thickness and radius
physiology-laplace.about: the pressure a thin-walled tube or sphere can hold, from radius, wall thickness and wall strength
physiology-laplace.how: Proved, with NO INSTANCE anywhere in this project: no vessel radius, wall thickness or wall strength exists for any organism here. It is in this table so that a part it would constrain carries the chip that says which three numbers are missing — a law with no instance is a request for data, and silence about it is worse.

scaling-strength-law.label: Strength scales as L^2: the missing half of Galileo's square-cube argument (R7)
scaling-strength-law.about: breaking load under isometry: it scales as L squared while weight scales as L cubed
scaling-strength-law.how: The reason a design cannot simply be made bigger. Weight grows faster than the cross-section carrying it, so a part that holds at one size fails at another with no change in material or shape.

elastic-similarity.label: Elastic similarity scaling (not formalised)
elastic-similarity.about: scaling that holds elastic deflection constant instead of stress
elastic-similarity.how: NOT FORMALISED. The named alternative to isometry for real skeletons, so its absence is why every scaling chip here says `under isometry`.

scaling-area-law.label: Area law and wing loading under isometry (R2, R3)
scaling-area-law.about: area under isometry: A scales as L squared
scaling-area-law.how: If the design scales a lifting or exchange surface by changing a length, this fixes the area ratio it gets — under isometry, which is a hypothesis about the design, not a fact about the animal. The flying-fish audit returns `violated` here for skin and fins, because that fish is NOT isometric: the law is right and the hypothesis is false, which is the useful outcome.

scaling-bending-law.label: Bending strength of an isometric member via the section modulus (R9)
scaling-bending-law.about: bending stress in a cantilever as the body scales
scaling-bending-law.how: A wing or a leg held out from the body is a cantilever, and the stress at its root rises with size under isometry. This is the law that should be consulted first by anyone who wants to put a lifting surface on the end of a limb.

thompson1917-ch02-10.label: Speed varies as the square root of linear size in swimming, flight and walking
thompson1917-ch02-10.about: how minimum flight speed scales with size
thompson1917-ch02-10.how: A bigger animal of the same shape must fly faster to stay up. Combined with a launch speed the design declares, this is often what decides a flight claim.

flight-allometry-law.label: General allometry: measured exponents compose (W = a L^b)
flight-allometry-law.about: minimum speed from wing loading and a maximum lift coefficient
flight-allometry-law.how: The law behind `lifting_area_supports_mass`. It needs a maximum lift coefficient, which is where a design most often stops: the coefficient is a MEASURED property of a real wing, the table of them is scoped by clade, and borrowing one across clades is the failure that table exists to prevent.

flight-climb-glide-law.label: Climb from excess power and the range of a steady glide
flight-climb-glide-law.about: climb rate from excess power, and the horizontal range of a steady glide from a height
flight-climb-glide-law.how: Scope.taxa is `any`: it is a theorem about a model and applies wherever the design supplies the quantities and accepts the hypotheses. That makes it the most portable flight law here — and it is about a GLIDE. Powered flight is a power question and goes to the aerobic bound.

aspect-ratio-induced-drag.label: Induced drag falls with wing aspect ratio (not formalised)
aspect-ratio-induced-drag.about: induced drag falling with aspect ratio
aspect-ratio-induced-drag.how: NOT FORMALISED. Without it, nothing here distinguishes a long narrow wing from a short broad one of the same area, which is most of what a wing design IS.

genotype-pleiotropy-closure.label: An edit to a gene must be shown changing every node the map links that gene to
genotype-pleiotropy-closure.about: what a view of a genotype may omit: that the set shown is closed under the declared pleiotropy relation
genotype-pleiotropy-closure.how: A statement about the COMPLETENESS OF A VIEW, not about development. If a molecule is shown as affecting one part, this is what certifies that its other declared effects were not quietly dropped from the picture — which is exactly the failure a per-part panel invites.

genotype-genetic-code.label: A claimed amino-acid change is impossible below the code distance
genotype-genetic-code.about: what a claimed set of substitutions rules out, given the genetic code
genotype-genetic-code.how: Operates on a claimed edit. For a construct with an unedited donor genome there is nothing for it to operate on, and that is the honest answer rather than a refusal.

gene-regulatory-dynamics.label: Gene regulatory dynamics (not formalised)
gene-regulatory-dynamics.about: the dynamics of a regulatory network
gene-regulatory-dynamics.how: NOT FORMALISED, and it is the hole the whole scale ladder sits over. Nothing in the Lean set connects a molecule to a tissue. The ladder's molecular rungs are therefore LITERATURE, graded and quoted, and the theatre must never draw them in the same colour as a proof.

muscle-power-premise.label: Thompson's muscle-power premise P = f p M (retired)
muscle-power-premise.how: STATED, NOT PROVED: a named hypothesis (MusclePowerLaw in lean/Delphi/Scaling.lean), replaced for the Studio by the aerobic bound. A chip for it must read as an assumption, because that is all it is.

numbers.froude: Equal Froude number is a NECESSARY condition for two animals to move in a dynamically similar way, and later work is explicit that it is not sufficient -- cursorial and non-cursorial mammals do not move similarly at equal Fr. The widely quoted walk-to-run transition at Fr = 0.5 is a human result. Turning any of that into a pass or a fail for an arbitrary clade would be borrowing a threshold across exactly the gap this repository keeps finding and removing, so this check reports the number and stops.

That needs a coefficient measured through a wingbeat and a muscle power density for the clade, and this repository has neither.). numbers.reason: a steady maximum lift coefficient is the WRONG QUANTITY for Drosophila melanogaster, which the NCBI taxonomy places inside Insecta. This is a decision, not a missing measurement: NOT a missing measurement. A steady maximum lift coefficient is the wrong quantity for a flapping insect wing, and adding one would answer the question with a model its own source says does not apply. Dickinson, Lehmann and Sane measured forces on a dynamically scaled robotic Drosophila melanogaster wing and reported that the enhanced aerodynamic performance of insects comes from three interacting mechanisms -- delayed stall during the translational phase, and rotational circulation and wake capture during stroke reversals. The second and third exist only because the wing rotates and reverses, and a steady coefficient represents neither. Using one here would compute a lift that omits a large part of where an insect's lift actually comes from, and present the shortfall as a property of the animal. A right answer needs a quasi-steady model with translational, rotational and added-mass terms, and the wing kinematics to drive it; or a measured force trace through the wingbeat, which is what the robotic-wing experiments produce; either way a stroke amplitude, a wingbeat frequency and an angle-of-attack schedule, none of which this repository holds for any insect. Source: Dickinson MH, Lehmann FO, Sane SP 1999, Wing rotation and the aerodynamic basis of insect flight, Science 284(5422):1954-1960 (doi 10.1126/science.284.5422.1954).
numbers.why_this_matters: Dickinson, Lehmann and Sane showed on a dynamically scaled robotic Drosophila wing that an insect gets a large part of its lift from rotational circulation and wake capture, which exist only because the wing reverses. A steady maximum lift coefficient represents neither. Borrowing the flying fish or the sugar glider would have produced a number; adding an insect number would have produced a number too, and both would be answering with a model the source says does not apply. The table therefore records Insecta as INAPPLICABLE with what a right check would need, which is a different claim from a missing measurement and sends a caller somewhere different.

THE ONTOLOGY BARELY PLACES THIS BODY IN THIS ORGANISM. Of 131 parts the blueprint returned, 2 have an in_taxon restriction specific enough to be evidence that Drosophila melanogaster has them; 44 are restricted only to a clade containing most of the animal kingdom, and 85 carry no restriction at all. The blueprint keeps a part unless a constraint removes it, so most of what is drawn here is unevidenced rather than wrong.
No part in this view has measured geometry. Every position is a declared slot in sim-engine/scales/body-frames.json, and a shape is a primitive, not a morphology.

taxon_audit.headline: Of 131 parts: 2 placed specifically, 44 placed only vacuously, 85 unconstrained, 0 contested, 0 forbidden. Only the first number is evidence that a part belongs in Drosophila melanogaster.
taxon_audit.what_it_shows: Taxon constraints cannot do the work the blueprint layer asks of them. The blueprint keeps a part unless a constraint removes it, and for the great majority of parts the ontology either says nothing at all or says only that the part occurs somewhere in a clade containing most of the animal kingdom. That is why a fruit fly came back with bone marrow and a preen gland and without a brain: nothing in the pipeline was ever in a position to object.

blueprint-well-formedness.label: An emitted anatomical blueprint graph is well-formed under its own rules
blueprint-well-formedness.about: the part graph itself: that each term is a node, each parent relation is one Uberon or CL relation, and the graph has no cycle
blueprint-well-formedness.how: Structural only. It certifies that the blueprint is a well-formed graph over ontology terms — it says nothing about whether the part could exist, work, or bear a load. It is the one law in the set that reaches every part of every organism, and the weakest thing anyone could want to know about any of them.

thompson1917-ch03-07.label: Weight tends to vary as the cube of linear dimensions during growth
thompson1917-ch03-07.about: the slope of log mass against log length is 3 under isometry
thompson1917-ch03-07.how: The cube law as an exponent, which makes it testable: a measured slope that is not 3 is a measurement of how the organism departs from isometry. E1 is the observation that this project's fish do depart.

altitude-coupling.label: Demand rises and supply falls with height together, so the flyable heights reach down to the ground
altitude-coupling.about: that the feasible set is downward closed in altitude: feasible high implies feasible low
altitude-coupling.how: Couples the two layers: thinner air both reduces lift and reduces oxygen, so a design feasible at altitude is feasible below it. Useful mainly as a sanity direction on a scenario sweep.

physiology-q10.label: Q10 temperature scaling: the ratio between two temperatures is Q10 raised to their difference over ten
physiology-q10.about: how a rate changes with a ten-degree change in temperature
physiology-q10.how: Proved, no instance: no candidate commits a Q10 and the conditions file fixes 25 C. Every rate in every run is therefore at one temperature, and a design whose selling point is a rate should say which temperature it means.

genotype-developmental-ordering.label: No structure develops from a precursor that appears later than it does
genotype-developmental-ordering.about: that a claimed developmental ordering has no cycle and respects the dependencies declared for it
genotype-developmental-ordering.how: The only law in the set that is about TIME, which makes it the one the time-lapse rests on. It certifies that an ordering is consistent; it does not supply one, does not predict a rate, and says nothing about how long a stage takes. A developmental animation is therefore a declared ordering being checked for consistency, never a simulation of development.

E2.label: The fitted mass exponent lies in [2.90, 3.02]
E2.about: a measured band for the weight ratio
E2.how: A measured band from one species. Outside that species it is a number, not a constraint.

E7.label: A lever lethal before the scoring stage cannot produce the phenotype
E7.about: that a trait appearing after a lethal stage cannot be scored
E7.how: The other law about time, and the one that matters most for a time-lapse: a part that appears after the organism would have died is not a part. Pairs with the developmental ordering law.

physiology-laplace.label: Laplace wall stress: pressure in a thin-walled vessel is limited by wall strength, thickness and radius
physiology-laplace.about: the pressure a thin-walled tube or sphere can hold, from radius, wall thickness and wall strength
physiology-laplace.how: Proved, with NO INSTANCE anywhere in this project: no vessel radius, wall thickness or wall strength exists for any organism here. It is in this table so that a part it would constrain carries the chip that says which three numbers are missing — a law with no instance is a request for data, and silence about it is worse.

scaling-strength-law.label: Strength scales as L^2: the missing half of Galileo's square-cube argument (R7)
scaling-strength-law.about: breaking load under isometry: it scales as L squared while weight scales as L cubed
scaling-strength-law.how: The reason a design cannot simply be made bigger. Weight grows faster than the cross-section carrying it, so a part that holds at one size fails at another with no change in material or shape.

elastic-similarity.label: Elastic similarity scaling (not formalised)
elastic-similarity.about: scaling that holds elastic deflection constant instead of stress
elastic-similarity.how: NOT FORMALISED. The named alternative to isometry for real skeletons, so its absence is why every scaling chip here says `under isometry`.

scaling-area-law.label: Area law and wing loading under isometry (R2, R3)
scaling-area-law.about: area under isometry: A scales as L squared
scaling-area-law.how: If the design scales a lifting or exchange surface by changing a length, this fixes the area ratio it gets — under isometry, which is a hypothesis about the design, not a fact about the animal. The flying-fish audit returns `violated` here for skin and fins, because that fish is NOT isometric: the law is right and the hypothesis is false, which is the useful outcome.

scaling-bending-law.label: Bending strength of an isometric member via the section modulus (R9)
scaling-bending-law.about: bending stress in a cantilever as the body scales
scaling-bending-law.how: A wing or a leg held out from the body is a cantilever, and the stress at its root rises with size under isometry. This is the law that should be consulted first by anyone who wants to put a lifting surface on the end of a limb.

thompson1917-ch02-10.label: Speed varies as the square root of linear size in swimming, flight and walking
thompson1917-ch02-10.about: how minimum flight speed scales with size
thompson1917-ch02-10.how: A bigger animal of the same shape must fly faster to stay up. Combined with a launch speed the design declares, this is often what decides a flight claim.

flight-allometry-law.label: General allometry: measured exponents compose (W = a L^b)
flight-allometry-law.about: minimum speed from wing loading and a maximum lift coefficient
flight-allometry-law.how: The law behind `lifting_area_supports_mass`. It needs a maximum lift coefficient, which is where a design most often stops: the coefficient is a MEASURED property of a real wing, the table of them is scoped by clade, and borrowing one across clades is the failure that table exists to prevent.

flight-climb-glide-law.label: Climb from excess power and the range of a steady glide
flight-climb-glide-law.about: climb rate from excess power, and the horizontal range of a steady glide from a height
flight-climb-glide-law.how: Scope.taxa is `any`: it is a theorem about a model and applies wherever the design supplies the quantities and accepts the hypotheses. That makes it the most portable flight law here — and it is about a GLIDE. Powered flight is a power question and goes to the aerobic bound.

aspect-ratio-induced-drag.label: Induced drag falls with wing aspect ratio (not formalised)
aspect-ratio-induced-drag.about: induced drag falling with aspect ratio
aspect-ratio-induced-drag.how: NOT FORMALISED. Without it, nothing here distinguishes a long narrow wing from a short broad one of the same area, which is most of what a wing design IS.

genotype-pleiotropy-closure.label: An edit to a gene must be shown changing every node the map links that gene to
genotype-pleiotropy-closure.about: what a view of a genotype may omit: that the set shown is closed under the declared pleiotropy relation
genotype-pleiotropy-closure.how: A statement about the COMPLETENESS OF A VIEW, not about development. If a molecule is shown as affecting one part, this is what certifies that its other declared effects were not quietly dropped from the picture — which is exactly the failure a per-part panel invites.

genotype-genetic-code.label: A claimed amino-acid change is impossible below the code distance
genotype-genetic-code.about: what a claimed set of substitutions rules out, given the genetic code
genotype-genetic-code.how: Operates on a claimed edit. For a construct with an unedited donor genome there is nothing for it to operate on, and that is the honest answer rather than a refusal.

gene-regulatory-dynamics.label: Gene regulatory dynamics (not formalised)
gene-regulatory-dynamics.about: the dynamics of a regulatory network
gene-regulatory-dynamics.how: NOT FORMALISED, and it is the hole the whole scale ladder sits over. Nothing in the Lean set connects a molecule to a tissue. The ladder's molecular rungs are therefore LITERATURE, graded and quoted, and the theatre must never draw them in the same colour as a proof.

muscle-power-premise.label: Thompson's muscle-power premise P = f p M (retired)
muscle-power-premise.how: STATED, NOT PROVED: a named hypothesis (MusclePowerLaw in lean/Delphi/Scaling.lean), replaced for the Studio by the aerobic bound. A chip for it must read as an assumption, because that is all it is.

universal_laws.because: the quantities are there and no check in this run evaluated this law against them

links.experiment_type: homologous-recombination null mutant, lifespan assay in two genetic backgrounds and both sexes

source.title: Molecular evolution and functional characterization of Drosophila insulin-like peptides

links.quote: mutant males, demonstrating that DILP2 is limiting for lifespan in both sexes.
links.what_it_does_not_show: The effect is small (8-13% median in females, 9% in males). The same paper shows the dilp2-3,5 triple mutant is NOT long-lived without Wolbachia, i.e. the mapping from dilp dosage to lifespan is non-monotonic and depends on an endosymbiont, which no part of this ladder models.

missing_rungs.why: No source fetched in this run reports a hazard-RATE parameter for any of these genotypes. Every link except l15 reports median or maximum lifespan, and l15's statement ('reduced late age-specific mortality') is qualitative and was read in an abstract only. The run's performance layer needs an intrinsic hazard; nothing here supplies a number for it.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A demographic study fitting Gompertz (or Gompertz-Makeham) parameters A and B to large cohorts of a defined long-lived genotype and its matched control, with the fitted values reported, so that a genotype edit can be mapped to a change in baseline hazard rather than to a percentage change in median lifespan.

missing_rungs.why: On the strongest tissue-restricted arm (dFOXO in median neurosecretory cells, l08) the mediator is explicitly unknown: Alic 2014 found no significant change in dilp2, dilp3 or dilp5 mRNA, so the DILP2 route established in l05-l07 is not the route used there, and the signal is called 'as-yet-unidentified'.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: An unbiased secretome or haemolymph proteomic comparison of mNSC>dfoxo flies versus controls, followed by RNAi of each candidate in the mNSCs to test whether it is required for the lifespan extension.

missing_rungs.why: No direct biochemical demonstration of InR-to-dFOXO signalling in Drosophila was obtained. The canonical paper (Puig et al. 2003, Genes Dev) is not open access: Europe PMC fullTextXML returned HTTP 500 and the NCBI PMC efetch body states that the publisher does not allow full-text XML download. Jünger 2003 (l01, l03) is genetic epistasis plus localisation, not kinase biochemistry, and its 14-3-3 statement cites mammalian work.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Access to Puig et al. 2003 (or equivalent open-access Drosophila work) showing phospho-site-specific dFOXO regulation by dPKB/Akt downstream of InR, with reporter or ChIP evidence for the target genes.

missing_rungs.why: The whole TOR arm (l11-l13) has no cell, cell_cell, tissue or organ rung at all. Rapamycin was fed to whole animals and the 4E-BP null is constitutive and ubiquitous. Nothing fetched in this run places TOR-dependent lifespan control in a named Drosophila tissue.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Tissue-restricted, adult-onset TORC1 manipulation (for example fat-body-, gut- or neuron-specific Tor RNAi or Rheb/TSC manipulation under GeneSwitch control) with lifespan readout.

missing_rungs.why: The 'cell' rung is never actually resolved to cells. Every fat-body result is qPCR, western blot or immunoassay on dissected tissue or whole flies, with the cell type inferred from a GAL4 driver's reported expression pattern rather than measured per cell.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Single-cell or single-nucleus RNA-seq of adult fat body and brain under the same dfoxo induction, so that the responding cell populations (and the fraction of them responding) are measured rather than assumed from a driver.

missing_rungs.why: Nothing fetched connects any of this mechanism to EXTRINSIC mortality. The run's performance layer caps expected life in the wild at 12.5 days through extrinsic hazard; every experiment cited here was done in vials with food, no predation and no weather, so the ladder explains only the intrinsic term and cannot predict the 1.09x wild outcome.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Field or mesocosm survival data for a reduced-IIS Drosophila genotype against a matched control under natural extrinsic mortality, or at minimum a laboratory hazard decomposition under imposed extrinsic mortality.

missing_rungs.why: Sex specificity is unexplained and unmodelled. Giannakou 2004 reports fat-body dFOXO extends female but not male life-span, Bai 2012's dilp6 effects are female-only, Alic 2014's experiments are female-only, and Bjedov 2010 reports a smaller rapamycin effect in males. A design requirement stated as 'a longer lifespan' is therefore under-specified.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Matched male and female cohorts for each tissue-restricted intervention, and a mechanistic account of the sex difference (for example whether the fat-body-to-brain DILP6/DILP2 circuit operates in males at all).

missing_rungs.why: ADDED BY VERIFICATION. The cell_cell -> tissue rung is circular and reverses direction. l05 leaves the fat body cell (CL_0000565) and lands on the fat-body-to-IPC interaction; l06 then lands that interaction back on FBbt_00003209, adult fat body - the same tissue the walk departed from one rung earlier - and points the arrow fat-body-ward, against the fat-body -> brain direction of l05 and l07. So the walk formally advances a level while physically standing still, and the single link that carries the whole ladder across this level (l06, Hwangbo 2004) is 'abstract only' because the paper is not open access. Every other rung on the walkable path has full text behind it; this one does not.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A full-text, tissue-restricted source whose cell-cell step lands on a tissue the chain has not already used - for example a brain or neurosecretory-tissue readout downstream of the fat body DILP6 signal - so that the cell_cell rung carries the walk forward rather than back onto its own origin.

missing_rungs.why: ADDED BY VERIFICATION. FBbt_00003209 (adult fat body) occupies BOTH the tissue rung (l06 target, l07 source) and the organ rung (l09 source). One ontology id standing at two consecutive levels means the tissue -> organ step is not a real level transition for the fat body arm; l09's note states the fly fat body is both, but the consequence - that the ladder has six distinct entities across seven rungs - was not recorded as a break.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Either a source that resolves the fat body into a sub-tissue with its own id (adult head / pericerebral versus abdominal fat body; the pericerebral term was searched for in ubergraph_labels4.json and not found), or an explicit decision to collapse tissue and organ into one rung for this organism and re-state the ladder as six levels.

downgraded.why: The quote is the second half of a model statement. checks.body: GBIF holds 4,503 occurrence records for Drosophila melanogaster Meigen, 1830, concentrated in KR, US, SE. In Greater Boston GBIF holds 58,684 records; the 10 most-recorded non-Aves species are listed. None of the 29 taxa GloBI records as eating Drosophila melanogaster Meigen, 1830 appear in this box's top 10 by record count. Read that as a gap in two databases before reading it as an empty niche: the box list is truncated, record-ranked and missing every Aves species. No population parameters were declared, so whether this design could establish against what is there has NOT been evaluated. That question needs numbers no occurrence database contains.

numbers.recorded_range: GBIF holds 4,503 occurrence records for Drosophila melanogaster Meigen, 1830, concentrated in KR, US, SE.
numbers.relationships_note: Grouped from GloBI's own interaction types. 28 taxa recorded eating this clade, 14 recorded parasitising it, 3 in a recorded mutualistic or symbiotic relationship with it, 13 it is recorded hosting. COMPETITION IS NOT AMONG THEM, and that is not an oversight: competition is the one ecological relationship that leaves almost no direct observational trace, because it is two organisms NOT doing something to each other. GloBI records interactions that somebody watched happen. Nobody watches an exclusion. Types this grouping does not recognise, left in "other": hasParasitoid.
numbers.predation_pressure: None of the 29 taxa GloBI records as eating Drosophila melanogaster Meigen, 1830 appear in this box's top 10 by record count. Read that as a gap in two databases before reading it as an empty niche: the box list is truncated, record-ranked and missing every Aves species.
numbers.the_sideways_point: GloBI records real predators of this clade with studies behind them. What it cannot give is a predation RATE, and a lifespan question needs a rate: an organism that lives twice as long in a jar may live no longer at all in a place where something eats it every week. The layer supplies the list and refuses the rate.

THE ONTOLOGY BARELY PLACES THIS BODY IN THIS ORGANISM. Of 131 parts the blueprint returned, 2 have an in_taxon restriction specific enough to be evidence that Drosophila melanogaster has them; 44 are restricted only to a clade containing most of the animal kingdom, and 85 carry no restriction at all. The blueprint keeps a part unless a constraint removes it, so most of what is drawn here is unevidenced rather than wrong.
No part in this view has measured geometry. Every position is a declared slot in sim-engine/scales/body-frames.json, and a shape is a primitive, not a morphology.

taxon_audit.headline: Of 131 parts: 2 placed specifically, 44 placed only vacuously, 85 unconstrained, 0 contested, 0 forbidden. Only the first number is evidence that a part belongs in Drosophila melanogaster.
taxon_audit.what_it_shows: Taxon constraints cannot do the work the blueprint layer asks of them. The blueprint keeps a part unless a constraint removes it, and for the great majority of parts the ontology either says nothing at all or says only that the part occurs somewhere in a clade containing most of the animal kingdom. That is why a fruit fly came back with bone marrow and a preen gland and without a brain: nothing in the pipeline was ever in a position to object.

verdicts.placed: some in_taxon restriction includes this organism
verdicts.contested: there IS an in_taxon restriction and none includes this organism -- a defect in the blueprint
verdicts.placed-vacuously: the only in_taxon restriction is to a clade in the top third of this organism lineage -- true of it and of most animals, so it discriminates nothing
verdicts.unconstrained: no in_taxon restriction exists, so the ontology is silent; not a defect and not a licence
verdicts.forbidden: never_in_taxon asserts this part cannot be in this organism

3.what_it_taught: 29 taxa are on record as eating this clade -- damselflies, orb-weavers, dragonflies, bush-crickets -- each traceable to a study. That is the nearest this system gets to the question, and it is not very near: a list of predators is not a mortality rate, and without a rate a longer intrinsic lifespan is not a longer life.

lands_on.label: adult fat body

chain_links.downgrade_reason: Read is 'abstract only' and the quote reports a gain-of-function result: activating dFOXO in pericerebral fat body reduces dilp-2 expression and represses insulin-dependent signalling. That is 'gain of function changes it' = `sufficiency` under genotype/AGENT_BRIEF.md. No pathway step is shown in the quotable text - no binding, reporter, epistasis, rescue or recording - and the full text was never obtained, so `mechanism` was not supported by anything fetched in this run.
chain_links.experiment_type: fat-body-restricted overexpression of dFOXO; dilp-2 expression and insulin-dependent signalling readout in peripheral fat body

source.title: Drosophila dFOXO controls lifespan and regulates insulin signalling in brain and fat body

chain_links.quote: We further show that this limited activation of dFOXO reduces expression of the Drosophila insulin-like peptide dilp-2 synthesized in neurons, and represses endogenous insulin-dependent signalling in peripheral fat body.
chain_links.what_it_does_not_show: Abstract only; the paper is not open access, so the actual assays, effect sizes and controls were not read in this run. It establishes a tissue-wide change in pathway state but no mediator.
